ANA.name: Anaheim Ducks
text: The Ducks are 10-8-1 so far.
If anything the record is kind: they’ve been outchanced more often than not.
Night to night, they pounce on turnovers and give up dangerous chances.
They create chances even when shorthanded.

BOS.name: Boston Bruins
text: The Bruins are 13-5-1 so far.
They’ve earned it, too, with the better of the chances in twelve of their 19 games.
Night to night, they leave most of the shooting to the forwards and sit back rather than forecheck.
Their goaltending has been stealing games.

BUF.name: Buffalo Sabres
text: The Sabres are 8-7-4 so far, losers of three straight.
That’s about how they’ve played, too: some nights on top, some not.
Their game? They rarely block shots and send their defensemen in to shoot.

CGY.name: Calgary Flames
text: The rebuild grinds on in Calgary: no playoffs in four seasons, and a 8-10-1 start.
And honestly, they haven’t played much better than that.
Night to night, they settle for a lot of hopeful shots and play fast, wide-open games.
They spend a lot of time in the box and their power play has no bite.

CAR.name: Carolina Hurricanes
text: The defending champs are picking up right where they left off, 15-3-2 out of the gate, winners of three straight.
They’ve earned it, too, with the better of the chances in 18 of their 20 games.
Expect them to spend most of the night in the other team’s end and give up dangerous chances.
They create chances even when shorthanded and their penalty kill is airtight.

CHI.name: Chicago Blackhawks
text: The rebuild grinds on in Chicago: no playoffs in six seasons, and a 5-13-1 start.
And honestly, they haven’t played much better than that.
Their game? They spend a lot of the night in their own end and find a way to get their shots past the blockers.
Their power play has no bite.

COL.name: Colorado Avalanche
text: Same old Avalanche: 11-6-3, and in the mix again.
The play has been closer than the record, though.
Night to night, they send their defensemen in to shoot and shoot from distance.
Their penalty kill is airtight.

CBJ.name: Columbus Blue Jackets
text: The rebuild grinds on in Columbus: no playoffs in six seasons, and a 7-10-0 start, losers of three straight.
And honestly, they haven’t played much better than that.
On the ice, they send their defensemen in to shoot and hound the puck in the other team’s end.
Their penalty kill leaks.

DAL.name: Dallas Stars
text: The Stars are 10-6-2, which is what we’ve come to expect.
The play has been closer than the record, though.
On the ice, they get in front of a lot of shots and grind games down.
Their power play is lethal and their penalty kill is airtight.

DET.name: Detroit Red Wings
text: The rebuild grinds on in Detroit: no playoffs in ten seasons, and a 7-10-3 start, losers of five straight.
They’ve played better than that, though, so a bit of luck could turn it around.
Night to night, they get in front of a lot of shots and ice the puck a lot to get out of trouble.
They stay out of the box and their power play is lethal.

EDM.name: Edmonton Oilers
text: The Oilers are 14-3-3, which is what we’ve come to expect, winners of three straight.
The play has been closer than the record, though.
Night to night, they lean hard on their top players and send their defensemen in to shoot.
Their power play is lethal.

FLA.name: Florida Panthers
text: After missing the playoffs last spring, the Panthers have bounced back to 11-7-2.
The play has been closer than the record, though.
Night to night, they rarely block shots and hound the puck in the other team’s end.
Their penalty kill is airtight and their power play is lethal.

LAK.name: Los Angeles Kings
text: The Kings have made the playoffs five years running, but they’re 5-10-2 this time, losers of three straight.
They’ve played better than that, though, so a bit of luck could turn it around.
Expect them to leave most of the shooting to the forwards and keep the other team to hopeful shots.
Their goaltending has let them down.

MIN.name: Minnesota Wild
text: The Wild are 14-3-4 so far.
They’ve earned it, too, with the better of the chances in twelve of their 21 games.
Night to night, they get pinned in their own end on long shifts and crash the net for second chances.
Their goaltending has been stealing games and they stay out of the box.

MTL.name: Montréal Canadiens
text: The Canadiens are 12-3-4 so far.
The play has been closer than the record, though.
On the ice, they get into a lot of chippy games and give up dangerous chances.
They spend a lot of time in the box, but their goaltending has been stealing games.

NSH.name: Nashville Predators
text: After missing the playoffs last spring, the Predators have bounced back to 11-4-5, winners of seven straight.
The play has been closer than the record, though.
Night to night, they get pinned in their own end on long shifts and keep things calm after the whistle.

NJD.name: New Jersey Devils
text: After missing the playoffs last spring, the Devils have bounced back to 14-6-0.
They’ve earned it, too, with the better of the chances in 16 of their 20 games.
Night to night, they play a finesse game and spend most of the night in the other team’s end.
They stay out of the box.

NYI.name: New York Islanders
text: After missing the playoffs last spring, the Islanders are 8-6-4.
That’s about how they’ve played, too: some nights on top, some not.
Night to night, they get caught after turnovers too often and roll all four lines.
Their goaltending has been stealing games, but their penalty kill leaks.

NYR.name: New York Rangers
text: After missing the playoffs last spring, the Rangers are 12-8-1.
That’s about how they’ve played, too: some nights on top, some not.
Night to night, they get right to the net and get a lot of their shots blocked.

OTT.name: Ottawa Senators
text: The Senators are 12-6-2 so far.
The play has been closer than the record, though.
Night to night, they rarely get burned after losing the puck and rarely get stuck out on long shifts.
Their goaltending has let them down.

PHI.name: Philadelphia Flyers
text: The Flyers are 5-10-6 so far.
And honestly, they haven’t played much better than that.
Their game? They get a lot of their shots blocked and grind games down.
They spend a lot of time in the box.

PIT.name: Pittsburgh Penguins
text: The Penguins are 7-10-2 so far.
They’ve played better than that, though, so a bit of luck could turn it around.
Their game? They sit back rather than forecheck and get to the dangerous chances.

SJS.name: San Jose Sharks
text: The rebuild grinds on in San Jose: no playoffs in seven seasons, and a 8-11-2 start.
And honestly, they haven’t played much better than that.
Their game? They ice the puck a lot to get out of trouble and shoot from distance.
Their power play has no bite and their penalty kill leaks.

SEA.name: Seattle Kraken
text: The Kraken are 9-7-1, still looking for their first playoff spot in three seasons.
If anything the record is kind: they’ve been outchanced more often than not.
Expect them to let the other team shoot, but mostly hopeful shots and roll all four lines.
Their penalty kill leaks and their power play has no bite.

STL.name: St. Louis Blues
text: After missing the playoffs last spring, the Blues are 9-8-2.
That’s about how they’ve played, too: some nights on top, some not.
Night to night, they keep things calm after the whistle and rarely get stuck out on long shifts.
Their power play has no bite.

TBL.name: Tampa Bay Lightning
text: Same old Lightning: 13-4-2, and in the mix again.
They’ve earned it, too, with the better of the chances in 13 of their 19 games.
Expect them to spend most of the night in the other team’s end and rarely block shots.

TOR.name: Toronto Maple Leafs
text: Last season was one to forget in Toronto, and this one hasn’t started much better: they’re 8-11-2, losers of five straight.
And honestly, they haven’t played much better than that.
On the ice, they pounce on turnovers and find a way to get their shots past the blockers.
They spend a lot of time in the box and their goaltending has let them down.

UTA.name: Utah Mammoth
text: The Mammoth are 10-8-2 so far, losers of four straight.
They’ve played better than that record, too, winning the battle for chances more often than not.
Their game? They rarely get stuck out on long shifts and collapse around the net and give up the point.
Their goaltending has let them down.

VAN.name: Vancouver Canucks
text: Last season was one to forget in Vancouver, and this one hasn’t started much better: they’re 3-17-1, losers of seven straight.
And honestly, they haven’t played much better than that.
Expect them to crash the net for second chances and spend a lot of the night in their own end.
Their penalty kill leaks and their goaltending has let them down.

VGK.name: Vegas Golden Knights
text: Last spring’s runners-up look hungry: they’re 13-5-3.
And it’s no mirage: they’ve had the better of the chances in 15 of their 21 games.
Expect them to get in front of a lot of shots and keep the other team to hopeful shots.
Their penalty kill is airtight and they create chances even when shorthanded.

WSH.name: Washington Capitals
text: After missing the playoffs last spring, the Capitals are 10-7-0.
That’s about how they’ve played, too: some nights on top, some not.
Their game? They get to the dangerous chances and get caught after turnovers too often.
Their goaltending has been stealing games.

WPG.name: Winnipeg Jets
text: After missing the playoffs last spring, the Jets are 9-8-3, winners of five straight.
That’s about how they’ve played, too: some nights on top, some not.
Night to night, they rarely get burned after losing the puck and find a way to get their shots past the blockers.
They create chances even when shorthanded.
